title: Choose the visual world for Uptime
question: The roll assigned Tide Table. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Tide Table
options.lineage: printed tide tables, nautical almanacs, ephemerides
options.thesis: A book of time you consult rarely and trust absolutely - exactly how this app is used.
options.viewport: One page of a tide table, edge to edge on chart stock, no cards. A running head with a hairline under it; the run set as the page's one headline figure in magenta overprint; an unbroken ticked scale beneath it carrying the milestones and a marker at now; then ruled two-column rows for began, best, window closes. The check-in is a dated stamp block, not a pill.
options.risk: A printed reference document can read as inert or bureaucratic - a spreadsheet instead of a game. Only the scale of the headline figure and the overprint keep it from being a form.

raised.raise: Ground commitment: the tinted stock owns the entire field at full strength, never a white app with a tint on its panels.
One unbroken line: the run scale spans the full width and never wraps, only scales, with a marker at now.
Colour only where it carries state: magenta and blue are reserved for the live run and banked time; every other mark is black on stock.
One rigid label grammar: every record - a friend, a board row, a gift - is the same ruled two-column entry, never a card.

options.label: The Passbook
options.lineage: bank savings passbooks, stamped ledger rows
options.thesis: Time as a balance you can see, deposit and withdraw, stamped row by row.
options.viewport: The inside spread of a savings book: the running balance as the one large figure, every gift a stamped ruled row with date and amount, withdrawals in red, the cover's foil rule framing the page.
options.risk: The most legible answer to 'time as currency', and therefore where most attempts at this product would land. Familiar by construction.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: The elapsed figure built cell by cell on a construction grid that stays visible.
options.viewport: The day count assembled from grid cells at monumental scale, the armature visible beneath it, small neutral grotesk for every label.
options.risk: Reads as a type exercise rather than a product when the figure is the only thing the grid ever builds.
options.case: Holds product clarity: a numeral that rebuilds cell by cell as it changes is genuinely apt for a ticking figure, and a visible grid suits a table world. Loses audience identification - modernist specimens are not this audience's native world.

options.label: Cracktro Queue
options.thesis: Rank is depth: nothing is ever enclosed by a rule or a box.
options.viewport: One bitmap line of the day count dead still on black, three dust fields drifting behind it, an amber caret at the head of the line.
options.risk: Permits one signal colour, and this product needs two distinguishable roles - the live run and the banked balance would collapse into each other.
options.case: Holds audience identification in the computing sense - 'uptime' is a sysadmin's word, and depth-as-rank is a real leaderboard mechanic that fights the card-stack rut hard. Loses product clarity on the single-accent constraint and on drift, which the motion budget cannot afford.

options.label: Step Row
options.thesis: Sixteen lit steps under a chase light that always says where now is.
options.viewport: The window as a sixteen-step row, the chase light sweeping toward the deadline.
options.risk: A sixteen-step loop implies repetition and tempo.
options.case: Loses product clarity decisively: a looping step row misrepresents a single unbroken 60-day span, and tempo implies frequency of action - exactly the daily-pressure model this product refuses.
options.kept: One unbroken line that never wraps, only scales, with a marker for now.

options.label: Copy-Shop Zine
options.thesis: Colour is the sheet, never the mark; one stock per page.
options.viewport: One typed column down a coloured sheet, the heading enlarged until its counters fill in.
options.risk: Copier degradation is hostile to a figure that must stay exactly legible.
options.case: Loses both: zine culture is not this audience's world, and a degraded display face actively fights a precise elapsed readout that changes every second.
options.kept: Ground commitment - colour owns the whole field at full strength, never accents on neutral.

options.label: Iridescent Cloud Edge
options.lineage: diffraction at a forming cloud edge
options.thesis: Colour confined to a narrow spectral band while the field stays achromatic.
options.viewport: An achromatic text field with a narrow mint-rose-violet fringe marking the active band.
options.risk: A pastel fringe cannot carry two strong, instantly distinguishable state roles.
options.case: Loses both: meteorological optics are not this audience's world, and a plain white ground with colour only at hairline edges is the soft default the calibration warns about.
options.kept: Colour allowed only where it carries state; everything else stays achromatic.

options.label: Sneaker Box Wall
options.thesis: A wall of end labels, each box pulled half out and hinged open.
options.viewport: A stacked wall indexed by end labels, the live one slid half out.
options.risk: A stack of discrete boxes cannot carry one continuous elapsed figure.
options.case: Loses product clarity: the home screen is a single unbroken span, and an index of discrete objects misrepresents it. Culturally adjacent to the audience, but the core screen fails.
options.kept: One rigid label grammar repeated on every item, never a bespoke card.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The dark streak dashboard: a big number in a ring, stat cards, progress bars - executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: What WHOOP and every streak app ships, at full craft. This is also what Uptime looks like today.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design - and you have already seen this one built.
